note: Uganda's large banks were tried for card terms: Stanbic Bank Uganda (the largest), Absa Bank Uganda, dfcu Bank and Bank of Africa Uganda; the Bank of Uganda's comparison of banks' rates and charges (1 April 2026) lists no card terms. Stanbic Bank Uganda's personal and private banking tariff guide (effective 27 March 2026), read in full: its credit card costs UGX 150,000 a year and UGX 22,600 to issue, charges 3% a month on the balance used, 3% on a domestic cash withdrawal, a UGX 30,000 late fee and a 4% currency conversion fee; the guide adds excise duty on its charges without stating the rate, so no tax is written; its table's text runs out of order, so its rows were matched by eye. dfcu Bank's tariff poster (effective 16 February 2026): its Visa Gold and Platinum credit cards in shillings cost UGX 120,000 and 200,000 a year for the primary card, charge 4% on a cash withdrawal (at least UGX 10,000), and 'Interest 42%' with no period stated; a yearly reading is likely (42% a month is no card's price), but as with Eswatini's, Tanzania's and Guinea-Bissau's cards no rate is written without its period, so dfcu's cards aren't written; the poster says every charge excludes 15% government excise duty. dfcu's late payment fee (10%, at least UGX 10,000) and over-limit fee (2%) don't say of what, so aren't written, nor is the 0.05% insurance, whose base isn't stated. Absa Bank Uganda's site lists no tariff guide (its candidate pages answered 404), and Bank of Africa Uganda's 2026-2027 tariff guide refused this client (403).
